answer: PoA resists sybil creation by requiring each identity to complete a Wesolowski-style VDF: repeated modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one. An attacker may run clone computations on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize the squaring chain for any one identity; every clone therefore incurs its own sequential delay. Like a raven reaching a copper ledge one step at a time, added hardware multiplies throughput, not speed per identity.
